title: Udham Singh, 1940
hook: a survivor of Jallianwala shot the former Punjab governor in London and was hanged

segments.voice: Yesterday, the robe for the general, and your line was outrage became reform. Did you speak up once about a wrong honor? Today, one man who carried Jallianwala Bagh for a very long time. Day nine hundred eighty-one.

London, 1940. A meeting hall in Westminster, full of officials and guests listening to speeches about India. Near the end, a man in the audience stands up, draws a revolver, and fires. Among those hit is Sir Michael O'Dwyer, who had been the lieutenant governor of Punjab when the troops fired at Jallianwala Bagh. O'Dwyer dies. The man with the gun is seized before he can leave the hall. His name is Udham Singh, and he has come a very long way, in miles and in years, to stand in that room.
screen: `A MEETING HALL IN LONDON.` → `A MAN STANDS AND FIRES.` → `HE IS SEIZED IN THE HALL.`

segments.voice: First, the memory. Udham Singh grew up in an orphanage in Amritsar. Sikh and Punjabi memory holds that he was at Jallianwala Bagh on the day of the firing, and that what he saw there never left him. Some historians question whether he was there, and the sources don't settle it. Either way, the lieutenant governor who had backed the general became, for him, the name of that day. Second, the years. He did not act quickly. He traveled, worked, was jailed, and eventually reached England. The shooting in London came long after the garden in Amritsar. That's today's line: a long memory. Third, the name. Accounts of his trial say that he gave his name as Ram Mohammad Singh Azad: a Hindu name, a Muslim name and a Sikh name together, and azad, which means free. He was tried, convicted and hanged in London. Fourth, how he's remembered. In Punjab he is honored as a shaheed, a martyr, and his ashes were later brought home. Others, then and since, have judged the killing differently, and the Sikh tradition itself teaches deep caution about anger. The name he chose points to something the Guru Granth Sahib says plainly. At Ang 1349, Bhagat Kabir sings that from one light the whole world came into being, so who can be called good and who bad? Whatever people conclude about his act, the name Udham Singh chose refused to divide the people of Punjab.
screen: `HE CARRIED THAT DAY WITH HIM.` · `THE YEARS BEFORE HE ACTED.` · `RAM MOHAMMAD SINGH AZAD.` · `FROM ONE LIGHT, THE WHOLE WORLD.` · then, large: `A LONG MEMORY.`

segments.voice: Two minutes with a long memory. Sit, and let your breath slow down. Bring to mind something from long ago that you still carry: a hurt, a loss, a day that changed things. Don't replay it. Just notice that you're still holding it. Breathe in, and notice whatever weight it has today. Breathe out, and let your hands rest open. You're not asked to forget, or to forgive on the spot. Only to sit beside the memory without letting it steer. If you pray, you can say Waheguru on each breath out. The bell holds the time.
Udham Singh. The man who, years after Jallianwala Bagh, shot Punjab's former lieutenant governor in London, gave his name as Ram Mohammad Singh Azad, and was hanged. Today's word.
Your line: a long memory. Today, ask an older person what they remember that the rest of the family has forgotten, and just listen. Day nine hundred eighty-one.

howItsDone: Udham Singh is honored in Punjab as a shaheed; his memorials, his name on public places and his anniversary are kept there, and his story is told alongside the memory of Jallianwala Bagh.
